channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: The effect of music therapy on function in people with Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies (3635 patients) found music therapy significantly improved athletic function (SMD = -0.53), balance (SMD = 0.45), gait (SMD = 0.59), depression (SMD = -0.76), anxiety (SMD = -0.59), sleep quality (SMD = -0.76), cognitive function (SMD = -0.90), and swallowing function (SMD = -1.35) in people with Parkinson's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Therapy Performance Predicts Functional Recovery After Stroke.
item.description: Therapy performance metrics (TPMs) extracted from clinical notes using machine learning predict functional discharge outcomes in stroke patients (n=42) as early as 5-7 days post-admission, with R² values of 0.64-0.78 for 10MWT, 6MWT, and BBS. Incorporating TPMs improved 6MWT prediction from R²=0.30 to 0.63, reducing error by ~25 m.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (348 patients) found action observation therapy (AOT) significantly improved cognitive function (SMD=0.86), activities of daily living (SMD=0.67), and naming aphasia (SMD=0.53) in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment. AOT also improved motor function (gait velocity SMD=0.70, TUG SMD=-1.05) in dementia patients without stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of the timing and setting of pulmonary rehabilitation on functional recovery after lung cancer surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found late-phase pulmonary rehabilitation significantly improved 6-minute walk distance (MD=68.86 m, 95% CI 53.46-84.26), peak oxygen uptake (MD=2.62 ml/kg/min), and FEV1 (MD=0.52 L) after lung cancer surgery. Early in-hospital rehabilitation did not reduce complications or shorten hospital stay. Partially supervised modes were comparable to fully supervised.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Adding Fatigue-Focused Cognitive Behavior Therapy to Supervised Pilates-Based Core Stability Training on Balance and Walking in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A double-blind RCT found adding cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to supervised Pilates-based core stability training significantly improved balance and gait more than Pilates alone. After 8 weeks, the study group showed greater reduction in overall stability index (mean difference -0.59, 95% CI: -0.70 to -0.48; p < .001) and increase in cadence (mean difference 8.22 steps/min, 95% CI: 4.40 to 12.04; p < .001) compared to the control group.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies (8 cohorts) on self-guided, home-based rehabilitation (SGHBR) for upper limb recovery in stroke patients found no significant advantage over other interventions, though the pooled estimate slightly favored SGHBR (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Selective distal upper extremity recovery following targeted dentate nucleus temporal interference stimulation in stroke-double-blind, sham-controlled randomized controlled trial with resting-state EEG
item.description: This double-blind, sham-controlled RCT of 50 subacute stroke patients found active cerebellar dentate nucleus-targeted transcranial temporal interference stimulation (DN-tTIS) combined with rehabilitation significantly improved FMA-UE (adjusted mean difference 3.98 points, p=0.006) and ARAT (adjusted mean difference 2.98 points, p=0.005), primarily driven by distal motor control (d=2.46, p<0.001). No serious adverse events occurred.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: A 6-month prospective cohort study (n=112) of stroke patients found stride time variability (STV) at discharge to be the only independent predictor of post-discharge falls. An optimal STV cutoff of 3.40% yielded an AUC of 0.756 (95% CI 0.657-0.851), with 88.2% sensitivity and 53.8% specificity for fall prediction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Improvement in functional movement, landing mechanics, and dynamic balance following TRX training in physically active athletes after ACL reconstruction: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial found a 6-week TRX suspension training program significantly improved dynamic balance (e.g., anterior reach: F=33.527, p<0.001), movement quality (FMS scores: F=251.994, p<0.001), and landing mechanics (LESS scores: F=75.385, p<0.001) more than traditional rehabilitation in male athletes after ACL reconstruction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=2548) on extended window IVT (4.
item.description: A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (n=2548) on extended window IVT (4.5-24 hours) for acute ischemic stroke found IVT significantly increased the odds of 90-day mRS 0-1 (OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.23-1.72). It also increased early neurological improvement (OR 1.59) but did not significantly improve 90-day mRS 0-2.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
item.description: A randomized crossover trial with chronic hemiparetic stroke patients found that VR-RAGT and screen-based AR-RAGT acutely modulated paretic gait mechanics differently, with sequential combined VR + AR producing the broadest modulation of muscle activation, limb loading, and COP progression.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Functional Visuo-Proprioceptive Stimulation on Upper- and Lower-Limb Motor Impairment After Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled crossover trial (N=21) found that functional visuo-proprioceptive stimulation (FPS) was associated with reduced upper-limb (7.22 points FMA-UE improvement) and lower-limb (2.23 points FMA-LE improvement) motor impairment in individuals with subacute stroke, with upper-limb gains reaching clinically important difference ranges.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 RCTs found low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391) in carpal tunnel syndrome, with pulsed mode superior for analgesia and continuous mode for grip strength.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Different Neuromuscular Training Modalities and Doses on Lower-Limb Injury Prevention in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 RCTs (27,663 participants) found neuromuscular training (NMT) associated with reduced lower-limb injury risk (RR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.64–0.82) in athletes. Structured and multidimensional programs showed favorable estimates, particularly in adolescents and young adults. Overall certainty of evidence was very low.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated walking cost in cerebral palsy
item.description: This study of 23 children with cerebral palsy (CP) and 10 typically developing peers found body-weight support significantly reduced net energetic cost, with a 3.5-fold greater effect in the CP group. Energetic cost in CP decreased by 41% to a level similar to typically developing participants, identifying gravitational support as a key biomechanical target.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: 3D Biomechanics of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries in Football: What We Have Learned in the Last Five Years.
item.description: This review synthesizes findings from five years of research on 3D biomechanics of ACL injuries in elite male football players (n=33). It highlights multiplanar knee rotations (flexion, abduction, internal/external rotation) and context-dependent whole-body kinematics leading to injury, proposing biomechanically informed mitigation strategies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploratory analysis of the impact of age stratification on outcomes of combined Salter osteotomy and femoral osteotomy in pediatric developmental dysplasia of the hip using a 3-year cutoff.
item.description: A retrospective study (n=65) comparing combined Salter osteotomy and femoral osteotomy for pediatric DDH found that patients under 3 years had superior acetabular index and center-edge angle changes (P<0.001), significantly more excellent Severin (97.1% vs. 74.2%, P=0.002) and McKay (97.1% vs. 64.5%) results, and lower avascular necrosis risk (0% vs. 12.9%, P<0.05) than those aged 3 years or older, despite older patients having more severe baseline dysplasia.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patients treated with rehabilitation alone after anterior cruciate ligament injury display greater muscle strength symmetry, yet lower absolute muscle strength normalized to bodyweight compared to reconstruction: A Cross-sectional study of 3,093 patients.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 3,093 ACL patients (2707 ACLR; 386 rehabilitation) found that those treated with rehabilitation alone had greater muscle strength symmetry at all follow-ups but lower absolute strength normalized to bodyweight in the uninjured limb. They also reported higher KOOS symptoms but inferior knee self-efficacy compared to ACLR patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative diagnostic utility of SPECT-CT versus MRI and CT in chronic low back pain.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (n=122 patients, 610 levels) found SPECT-CT positivity was moderately and independently associated with Modic changes (OR 6.40, 95% CI 3.09-13.27), Pfirrmann 4-5 (OR 17.27, 95% CI 3.80-78.46), and vacuum disc (OR 2.69, 95% CI 1.30-5.58) in chronic low back pain. However, findings were frequently discordant, with 60.7% of Pfirrmann 4-5 levels being SPECT-EP-negative.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Injury risk and physical therapy utilization following knee surgery in U.S. Army soldiers: a comparison of military and non-military treatment facilities.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (n=4924 U.S. Army soldiers) found that 75% sustained a subsequent injury within 1-3 years of knee surgery. Soldiers treated at non-military treatment facilities (32%) had higher injury rates (79% vs. 73%) and longer physical therapy duration (8.3 vs. 7.1 weeks; p = 0.038) compared to those treated at military treatment facilities (MTFs), with adjusted odds of subsequent injury being 1.22 (95% CI [1.04-1.44]) higher at non-MTFs.
item.author: PubMed
